review: 1:4 הָאָשֵׁם — 'the guilty one' used collectively for جِنْسَنَا الْعَاصِي الْأَثِيم; אָשֵׁם is the biblical adjective of guilt (Gen 42:21) and the line needs one word.
2:2 כּוֹס הַחֵמָה — 'the cup of wrath' (Isa 51:17, Jer 25:15); the Arabic كَأْسَ الْغَضَب is that image and the Hebrew keeps the fixed phrase.
3:1–3:2 בִּידֵי הָאָב הִפְקַדְתָּ / רוּחֲךָ — Luke 23:46 with Ps 31:6; the Arabic splits the line (الـ / ـرُّوحَ) because of a long word, and Hebrew cannot split, so the spirit sits on 3:2.
3:4 בְּהִקָּרֵעַ הַפָּרֹכֶת — 'when the veil was torn' (Matt 27:51); the infinitive construct with בְּ marks the moment, and פָּרֹכֶת is the temple word rather than a generic curtain.
4:3–4:4 repeats 1:1–1:2 verbatim, as the Arabic does.
